- **Period:** 1 to 29 August 2026, by Mexico local date. The data ends on 29 August, so 30 and 31 August are not included: this covers 29 days, not the full month.

- **Meaning:** 95% of those first attempts were answered in 1746 ms or less. For context, the median was 893 ms and the slowest attempt took 14850 ms.
- **How it was computed:** recomputed from the individual attempts in silver_payments (every percentile method I ran, exact, interpolated, observed-value and approximate, gives 1746 ms), not by averaging daily p95 values. questions.question: Why did the approval rate for debit cards in Colombia drop on 13 August 2026?
questions.answer:
**Why CO debit approval dropped on 13 Aug**

**What happened**
Final approval for domestic debit cards in Colombia (approved on the first attempt or after a retry, over payments sent; all times Bogota) fell from 14:00 on 13 Aug, when routing v14 (CHG-0813: '100% of CO domestic debit to Acquirer B (cost optimization, -40 bps)') moved all debit traffic from Acquirer A to Acquirer B. It recovered when v14 was rolled back to v13 at 12:10 on 14 Aug (CHG-0814, incident INC-0814).

**Window used**
13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10, from the routing change to its rollback, not the whole calendar day (which closed at 79.4% vs 87.2% on 12 Aug).
- 13:00 hour on 13 Aug: 77 payments, all on A, 85.7%. 14:00 hour: 56 payments, all on B, 73.2%.
- 12:00 hour on 14 Aug: 74 payments on A at 86.5%, 17 still on B at 76.5%. From 13:00 all traffic was on A (88 payments, 86.4%).

**Impact** (window vs previous 14 days, CO debit)
- Final approval 75.6% vs 86.5%: -10.95 pp on 1,004 payments. First-attempt approval 70.7% vs 84.6%.
- 759 approvals vs 869 expected at baseline: 110 approvals lost.
- 47,095.86 USD approved of 61,689.16 USD attempted: 6,354.2 USD of approved volume lost. Fees paid in the window: 1,186.03 USD.

**Cause: acquirer-side, in two linked parts**
1. Trigger: B took 100% of payments (0% in the baseline) and approved far less on the first attempt. B / routing v14 explain -10.95 pp of the -10.95 pp change.
2. Missing safety net: retries did not work for B's biggest decline, code 05 (Do not honor), so those declines stayed final. This matches the decline-mapping change CHG-0806 (6 Aug 08:00, 'Decline-code mapping v2.3 for Acquirer B: adds R65 handling'), whose description does not mention 05.

**Evidence**
- Not issuer-side: the top issuers fell together (baseline to window: CO-ISS-02 87.9% to 74.6%, CO-ISS-01 87.8% to 80.0%, CO-ISS-03 84.8% to 72.4%); the largest single-issuer contribution is CO-ISS-02 at -2.25 pp. In the 12:00 hour on 14 Aug, debit approved 86.5% on A and 76.5% on B.
- Declines that grew (first-attempt declines as % of payments, A in baseline vs B in window): 05 Do not honor 4.1% to 13.7%; 1A 3DS authentication required 1.1% to 5.2%. Insufficient funds (51) did not grow (4.2% to 3.8%).
- Retries: on B, 1A was retried 100.0% of the time and 53.9% recovered, but 05 was never retried (0 of 137, 0.0%) and is classified 'hard' under mapping v2.3. On A in the baseline, 05 was 'soft', 98.4% retried and 21.7% recovered. 05 is the only code seen on both acquirers that is classified and retried differently.
- Footprint of CHG-0806: in the cascade alerts for CO (all card types), B/05 retries fell from a healthy 100.0% baseline to 5.0% on 6 Aug (1 of 20) and 0.0% on every day from 7 to 14 Aug. On 13 Aug, while A still carried the traffic (until 14:00), A's 05 declines were still retried under the same v2.3 map (24 declines, 100.0% retried). Domestic debit only felt it from 14:00 on 13 Aug because it had 0 payments on B in the previous 14 days.
- Other changes: the CO change log from 3 Aug 00:00 to 15 Aug 00:00 lists only CHG-0806, CHG-0813 and CHG-0814, with no release, risk-rule change or partner notice.

**Recommended actions**
1. Keep CO debit on v13 / Acquirer A, as the rollback did; do not re-apply v14 as is.
2. Ask the owner of CHG-0806 to review code 05 for Acquirer B (hard and never retried, vs soft and retried on A) and the rest of the v2.3 map for B. Check the current state first: the alert table shows no B/05 alert for CO on 15-20 Aug and I did not check why.
3. Other CO traffic first routed to B had 05 retries off on every day from 6 to 14 Aug (the alert table is not split by card type); size and fix that too.
4. Before moving debit to B again, test with a small share and watch first-attempt approval against A and the retry rate per code; ask B why 05 and 1A declines were higher. Weigh the stated 40 bps saving against this loss (I did not size the saving).

**Not checked**
- How much of the 110 lost approvals comes from B's weaker first attempt versus the missing 05 retries (needs a what-if I did not run).
- Why B declines more on the first attempt (no acquirer-internal detail in the data).
- Hourly and daily figures are domestic debit only; the impact, issuer, decline and retry figures are CO debit as returned by the functions.

questions.answer:
**Start: 13 Aug 2026 at 14:00. End: 14 Aug 2026 at 12:10 (local time, Bogota, UTC-5).** The window lasted 1,330 minutes (22 h 10 min). **Start, 13 Aug 14:00**
- Change log: CHG-0813 (routing) at 14:00 local (19:00 UTC), 'Routing v14: 100% of CO domestic debit to Acquirer B'. The first payment routed on v14 was at 14:00:36.

- Final approval 75.6% vs 86.5% baseline (-10.95 pp). First-attempt approval 70.7% vs 84.6%.
- 759 approvals vs 869 expected at the baseline rate: 110 lost approvals and 6,354.20 USD of lost approved volume.

questions.question: How many approvals and how much approved volume in USD did the Colombia debit incident of 13-14 August 2026 cost?
questions.answer:
**The incident cost 110 approvals and USD 6,354.20 of approved volume** (Colombia, debit, domestic traffic, versus the 14 days before the window).

**Window used:** 13 Aug 2026 14:00 to 14 Aug 2026 12:10, Bogota local time. I sized this window and not the full calendar days 13-14 Aug, because the incident is bounded by two production changes in the change log: CHG-0813 at 14:00 on 13 Aug (routing v14, 100% of CO domestic debit to Acquirer B) and its rollback CHG-0814 at 12:10 on 14 Aug (v14 -> v13, incident INC-0814). - Approvals: 759 of 1,004 payments sent, vs 869 expected at the baseline rate, so 110 approvals lost.
- Approved volume: USD 47,095.86 approved out of USD 61,689.16 attempted; lost approved volume USD 6,354.20.

**Cut-off sensitivity:** ending the window at 12:00 instead of 12:10 gives 108 lost approvals and USD 6,219.53; ending it at 13:00 gives 110 and USD 6,667.90.

**Checks not run:** I only sized the window (hourly approval, change log for CO from 3 to 15 Aug 2026, drop impact). I did not run fn_approval_drivers, fn_decline_shift or fn_cascade_health, and I did not check the footprint of the decline-mapping changes for Acquirer B that appear in the log (CHG-0806 on 6 Aug and CHG-0815 on 15 Aug). questions.question: Why did Acquirer B stop recovering 'do not honor' declines through cascading after 6 August 2026?
questions.answer:
**Why Acquirer B stopped recovering 'Do not honor' (ISO 05) declines**

**What happened.** From 2026-08-06 13:00 UTC, Acquirer B's 'Do not honor' first-attempt declines stopped being retried on a second acquirer in MX and CO: the retried share fell from 100.0% to 0.0% in both countries. The cause is internal. Decline-mapping change CHG-0806 (map v2.3 for B, owner team normalization) reclassified code 05 for B from soft/retryable to hard (not retryable). Its description only says 'adds R65 handling', so the 05 effect is not documented there. Hotfix CHG-0815 (v2.3.1, 2026-08-15 13:00 UTC, 'R05 reclassified as soft and retryable'; the log's R05 is code 05 in the data) reversed it.

**Window used.** 2026-08-06 13:00 UTC to 2026-08-15 13:00 UTC (MX 07:00 to 07:00 local, CO 08:00 to 08:00 local), from CHG-0806 to CHG-0815, not whole calendar days. Baseline: the 14 days before the window start. Domestic traffic, B as first acquirer.

**Before and after (B, code 05)**

| | MX | CO |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline: declines retried on a second acquirer | 100.0% of 444 | 100.0% of 280 |
| Baseline: retried declines that were approved | 38.5% | 37.5% |
| Window: declines retried | 0.0% of 264 | 0.0% of 314 |
| Map class of 05, baseline -> window | soft -> hard (v2.3) | soft -> hard (v2.3) |

**Impact (same window)**

| | MX | CO |
|---|---|---|
| B/05 recoveries lost (estimate at baseline retry and recovery rates) | 101.7 approvals | 117.8 approvals |
| B/05 lost approved USD (estimate, baseline average recovered amount) | 7,176 | 9,605 |
| B/05 loss as pp of payments sent (23,446 MX, 20,983 CO) | 0.43 pp | 0.56 pp |
| Country final approval rate, baseline -> window | 86.7% -> 86.0% | 86.7% -> 86.0% |
| Country change, lost approvals, lost approved USD (fn_drop_impact) | -0.78 pp, 182, 16,263 | -0.77 pp, 161, 4,411 |

The stop is worth an estimated 0.43 pp of MX's -0.78 pp and 0.56 pp of CO's -0.77 pp. The country rows include everything else that moved, and the two USD lines use different bases, so do not compare them line by line. In CO, 148 of the 314 declines (55.5 of the 117.8 lost recoveries, USD 4,527) were on payments routed under v14, which sent all CO domestic debit to B from 2026-08-13 19:00 UTC until its rollback at 2026-08-14 17:10 UTC. v14 enlarged the exposure but did not start the problem.

**Who moved (fn_approval_drivers, same windows).** CO: acquirer B -0.82 pp (B's rate 85.3% -> 81.6%), A +0.05 pp. MX: B -0.54 pp (81.9% -> 79.1%), A -0.20 pp, C -0.04 pp. No issuer stands out (largest: CO-ISS-01 -0.33 pp, MX-ISS-06 -0.25 pp).

**Evidence**
- Mapping flip, CO daily series: on 2026-08-05, 23 declines, all retried (v2.2, soft, retryable). On 2026-08-06, 1 decline on v2.2 (retried), then 19 on v2.3 (hard, not retryable), none retried. Zero retried on every day through 2026-08-14. On 2026-08-15, 2 declines on v2.3 (none retried), then 18 on v2.3.1 (soft, retryable), all retried; 100.0% retried each day through 2026-08-29. MX has no cascade-alert day after 2026-08-14 (checked to 2026-08-29).
- The cascade alerts flagged B/05 in MX and CO on 9 consecutive days, 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-14 (CO: 313 declines, 1 retried = 0.3%; MX: 265 declines, 3 retried = 1.1%; baseline 100.0%). These are the only acquirer/reason pairs flagged between 2026-06-01 and 2026-08-29.
- Only B/05 changed: in the same window A (MX, CO) and C (MX) kept 05 soft and 100.0% retried, and every other B code that existed in the baseline kept its classification and retry rate.
- Not more declines and not an outage: B's 05 declines were 1.2% of all MX payments in both periods (-0.07 pp; 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-29 vs the 14 days before), and B's technical errors and timeouts moved only between -0.04 and +0.03 pp of payments. MX first-attempt approval barely moved (82.9% -> 82.8%) while final approval fell (86.7% -> 86.0%), which is the signature of lost recoveries. In CO the 05 share rose +0.32 pp (0.9% -> 1.2%), with 109 declines on 2026-08-13 and 60 on 2026-08-14 (the v14 days) against 14 to 27 per day on 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-12.

- Why v2.3 reclassified 05 is not in the data. Code 65 (Exceeds frequency limit) appears at B only after v2.3 (0 declines in the baseline; 28 in CO and 43 in MX in the window), mapped soft but 0.0% retried. I did not size whether retrying it would recover anything.

- Lost recoveries and USD are estimates. I set the window from the change timestamps and the daily series, not the hourly table. BR: no cascade alert (2026-06-01 to 2026-08-29) and no B rows in cascade health or decline shift (2026-08-07 to 2026-08-29).

**Recommended action**
1. Keep v2.3.1 (05 soft/retryable for B) and ask the normalization team to confirm it holds in MX and CO.
2. Gate decline-mapping releases: diff every code's soft/hard/retryable class per acquirer between versions, and check fn_cascade_health (baseline_mapped_as vs window_mapped_as, cascade rate) within hours of deploying.
3. Route gold_cascade_alerts_daily to on-call. B/05 was flagged on the first day (2026-08-06) and the hotfix landed 9 days later.
4. Decide whether code 65 should be retryable at B.

questions.question: What happened to approvals in Brazil on the morning of 21 July 2026?
questions.answer:
**What happened**
Approvals in Brazil fell for three hours on 21 July 2026, from 09:00 to 12:00 local time (UTC-3), which is 12:00-15:00 UTC, and were back to normal from 12:00. I sized that window, not the whole morning or day. Segment: Brazil domestic cards, credit and debit together, payments that reached an acquirer (Acquirers A and C); all rates are final approval rates (cascade recoveries included).

| Hour (local) | Payments | Final approval, 21 Jul | Same hour, 6-19 Jul | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 08:00 | 91 | 90.1% | 89.7% | +0.4 pp |
| 09:00 | 94 | 73.4% | 89.0% | -15.6 pp |
| 10:00 | 114 | 67.5% | 88.4% | -20.8 pp |
| 11:00 | 144 | 75.0% | 87.1% | -12.1 pp |

The 12:00 hour (166 payments) was -1.1 pp vs its baseline. From 06:00 to 08:59 approvals were at or above the usual level (+2.8, +3.4 and +0.4 pp); the earlier hours have only 6 to 21 payments each, too few to read. Both card types fell (09:00 hour: credit 78.1% vs 92.0%, debit 63.3% vs 82.1%, same-hour baseline).

**Impact** (window 09:00-12:00 local vs the 14 days before it, 29,494 payments)
- Final approval rate 72.2% vs 88.0%: -15.9 pp. First-attempt approval rate 67.9% vs 84.8%.
- 254 approvals on 352 payments vs 310 expected at the baseline rate: 56 approvals lost.
- Approved volume USD 18,348.27 of USD 25,469.1 attempted; lost approved volume USD 4,110.5.

**Cause: issuer side. Scheduled maintenance at issuer BR-ISS-03 (notice EXT-0721); the cascade could not recover it.**
- Who moved: BR-ISS-03's final approval rate fell from 88.5% (baseline) to 10.7% (window) on 56 payments, 15.9% of window traffic vs 13.8% in the baseline. That is -12.4 pp of the -15.9 pp. No other issuer moved the total by more than 1.8 pp (19 to 78 payments each).
- Both acquirers fell together (baseline to window): C 87.7% to 74.0% (-10.6 pp contribution), A 89.3% to 65.8% (-5.3 pp). All BR payments used routing rule v13 in both periods, so there was no routing mix change.
- Declines: code 91 'Issuer or switch unavailable', as a share of all payments, went from 0.3% to 10.2% at C (36 first-attempt declines) and from 0.1% to 2.6% at A (9). No other code rose by more than 1.5 pp.
- Retries did not help: code 91 failures were retried on the second acquirer 100% of the time, as in the baseline, but only 5.6% were recovered at C (baseline 43.4%) and 0.0% at A (baseline 46.4%), because the issuer itself was unavailable. No reason code changed its soft/hard classification, the window ran on decline map v2.2, and the cascade alerts table has no BR alert from 11 to 22 July.
- Timing: the change log has one BR entry, EXT-0721, logged at 08:45 local (11:45 UTC): 'Issuer BR-ISS-03 scheduled maintenance 12:00-15:00 UTC'. That is 09:00-12:00 Brazil time, the exact window of the drop.
- No internal change: from 1 to 21 July 2026 the log has no BR routing, release, rollback, risk-rule or decline-mapping change (its only other entry, CHG-0702, is MX only).

**Limits**
- The rest of the drop is thinly spread over other issuers (largest BR-ISS-02, -1.8 pp); I found no separate cause for it.
- The data shows the notice and the BR-ISS-03 collapse, not the issuer's internal status.
- Cross-border cards had only 6, 4 and 9 payments in the three hours, too few to read. I did not check checkout conversion (risk blocks, 3DS).
- The daily anomaly table did not flag 21 July (whole day, domestic, vs trailing 28-day baseline: credit 88.3% vs 91.0%, -2.6 pp; debit 77.9% vs 81.1%, -3.2 pp), because the three-hour dip is diluted over the day.

**Recommended action**
1. No rollback or acquirer escalation: nothing points to an acquirer or an internal change.
2. Ask the partner for earlier notice (this one was logged 15 minutes before the window began) and put announced issuer windows, converted from UTC to local time, on the monitoring calendar.
3. For confirmed issuer maintenance, evaluate pausing second-acquirer retries for code 91 on that issuer only (they recovered 5.6% and 0.0% instead of 43-46%), and tell merchants so they can offer another payment method.
4. Add an hourly issuer-level approval alert: the daily check missed this, and BR-ISS-03 carries 13.8% of BR domestic payments in the baseline.

questions.question: Why did conversion in Brazil fall on 18 and 19 June 2026?
questions.answer:
**Short answer.** Brazil's conversion fell because a new risk rule began blocking more payments before they reached any acquirer. Risk rules v3 (new card-velocity rule, CHG-0618) went live on 18 Jun at 09:00 Sao Paulo time (12:00 UTC), and the tuned v3.1 (CHG-0620) followed on 20 Jun at 15:00 (18:00 UTC). Conversion (approved / payment intents) was 83.5% on 18 Jun and 81.8% on 19 Jun, against 85.0% in the 14 days before. The cause sits in the risk engine, ahead of routing, so it is neither an acquirer-side nor an issuer-side decline, and the cascade (retry on a second acquirer) cannot recover it.

**Window sized.** 'Rule window' = 18 Jun 09:00 to 20 Jun 15:00 local (CHG-0618 to CHG-0620), compared with the 14 days 4-17 Jun, all Brazil traffic. The first 9 hours of 18 Jun were before the rule and the effect ran into the morning of 20 Jun, so I show calendar days for reference.

**Impact**

| Period (Brazil, local) | Intents | Conversion | Change | Risk-block share | Lost approvals | Lost approved USD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline 4-17 Jun | 31,121 | 85.0% | | 1.3% | | |
| Rule window | 5,542 | 82.5% | -2.52 pp | 3.5% | 140 | 6,775 |
| 18 Jun (full day) | 2,332 | 83.5% | -1.55 pp | 3.0% | 36 | 1,027 |
| 19 Jun (full day) | 2,595 | 81.8% | -3.27 pp | 4.0% | 85 | 5,375 |
| 18-19 Jun together | 4,927 | 82.6% | -2.45 pp | 3.5% | 121 | 6,402 |
| After the retune, 21-25 Jun | 10,440 | 84.9% | -0.10 pp | 1.4% | | |

Lost = shortfall versus baseline conversion applied to the same intents (USD at the baseline approved-USD ratio). Rows overlap (calendar days vs the rule window), so do not add them. pp changes are computed on unrounded rates.

**Evidence**
- **Risk stage.** In the rule window the share of intents blocked by risk rose 2.28 pp (1.3% to 3.5%), which is 2.28 of the 2.52 pp conversion drop and 127 more blocked payments than the baseline rate implies. They are outright blocks, not review timeouts (166 blocks and 8 timeouts on 18-19 Jun, vs 340 and 50 over the 14 baseline days). 3DS abandonment (1.4% to 1.5%) and payments sent but not approved (12.3% to 12.5% of intents) barely moved, and routed_without_valid_attempt was 0 every day 4-25 Jun.
- **Timing.** Risk-block share was 1.6% on 18 Jun 00:00-09:00 (311 intents, small sample), 3.5% while v3 was live, 1.5% in the 9 hours after v3.1 (979 intents) and 1.4% on 21-25 Jun, when conversion was back to 84.9%.
- **No other change.** fn_changes_near for Brazil (8 Jun 00:00 to 21 Jun 00:00 local) lists only CHG-0618 and CHG-0620, both risk rules; it returns no routing, release, decline-mapping or partner-notice change for Brazil in that period.
- **Acquirers and issuers did not drive it.** In the rule window, final approval of payments sent moved only 88.0% to 87.6% (-0.33 pp; 16 lost approvals, no approved USD lost on that measure). The largest driver effects were -0.50 pp (not 3DS-authenticated), -0.48 pp (issuer BR-ISS-01) and -0.37 pp (gaming), with no acquirer or routing version standing out. For 18-19 Jun no decline code grew by more than 0.15 pp, and cascade rates and decline mapping (v2.2) were unchanged for the 30 acquirer/code pairs with the largest movement.
- **Brazil only, broad footprint.** On 18-19 Jun the risk-block share barely moved in CO (1.3% to 1.4%) or MX (1.2% to 1.2%); MX conversion did dip (84.5% to 83.6%), which I did not investigate. In Brazil on the same days every card brand, card type, channel and Brazilian issuer rose (Visa and Mastercard 1.3% to 3.7%, Elo 1.2% to 2.1%), most in education (0.8% to 6.5%, merchant BR-M10) and travel (1.1% to 5.6%, BR-M06), least in food delivery (1.3% to 1.9%).

**Recommended actions**
1. Risk team: sample the payments blocked by v3 (18 Jun 09:00 to 20 Jun 15:00) to separate genuine fraud from good customers, starting with education, travel and digital subscriptions (1.3% to 3.9%).
2. Keep v3.1 under daily watch: risk-block share was 1.4% on 21-25 Jun against a 1.3% baseline (+0.12 pp).
3. Alert on risk-block rate and conversion by country, and release new risk rules in shadow mode first. A monitor on approval of payments sent would not show this (88.0% to 87.6%).

**Limits.** The data has no fraud or chargeback outcomes, so I cannot say how much fraud v3 stopped or net it against the 6,775 USD lost. It does not record which rule condition blocked each payment, so the link to v3 rests on timing, a risk-stage-only footprint and no other Brazil change in the period checked. Decline-code and cascade checks used 18-19 Jun, not the exact rule window.

questions.question: Which acquirer had the higher final approval rate on domestic credit cards in Mexico in July 2026, A or C, and by how much?
questions.answer:
Acquirer A had the higher final approval rate: 89.3% vs 88.6% for C, so A was ahead by about 0.7 percentage points (0.653 pp before rounding).

Segment and period: Mexico, credit cards, domestic only (is_cross_border = false), 1-31 July 2026 (local dates). Final approval rate = final approved / payments sent, including approvals recovered by a cascade retry; results are attributed to the first acquirer chosen by routing. Rates come from the summed monthly counts, not from an average of daily rates.

| Acquirer | Payments sent | Final approved | Final approval rate | First-attempt approval rate | Recovered by cascade |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 27,501 | 24,549 | 89.3% | 86.2% | 832 |
| C | 18,301 | 16,217 | 88.6% | 85.5% | 569 |

Supporting detail:
- A is also ahead on first-attempt approval (86.2% vs 85.5%).
- Day by day (1-31 July), A's final approval ranged from 87.3% (10 Jul) to 91.4% (13 Jul) and C's from 86.1% (7 Jul) to 91.4% (8 Jul). A was ahead on most days and C on some (for example 8 and 10 July), so the gap is spread across the month rather than coming from a single window. I see no multi-day drop for either acquirer in that daily series.

What I did not check: I did not run the cause checks (approval drivers, decline shift, cascade health, change log) or the anomaly and cascade-alert tables, and the comparison is not adjusted for traffic mix (issuer, card brand, merchant segment) or tested for statistical significance. So I am not attributing the gap to any cause. I can run those checks if you want to know why C trails A.

questions.question: Compare the first-attempt approval of Acquirers A and B on domestic debit cards in Mexico in July 2026.
questions.answer:
First-attempt approval, Acquirer A vs Acquirer B: domestic debit cards, Mexico, 1-31 July 2026 (local dates)

First-attempt approval = payments approved on the first attempt / payments sent, before any cascade retry. Payments are attributed to the first acquirer chosen by routing.

| | Acquirer A | Acquirer B |
|---|---|---|
| Payments sent | 15,130 | 15,148 |
| Approved on first attempt | 12,072 | 11,564 |
| First-attempt approval rate | 79.8% | 76.3% |
| Soft decline on first attempt | 15.6% | 17.5% |
| Hard decline on first attempt | 3.7% | 4.7% |
| Technical error or timeout on first attempt | 0.9% | 1.4% |

(Shares are of payments sent and may not add to 100% because of rounding.)

Acquirer A is 3.4 pp above Acquirer B (calculated on unrounded rates, so it can differ by 0.1 from the difference of the rounded figures). The 95% sampling margin on that gap is about +/-0.9 pp, so it is not noise. B is higher in all three failure categories; soft declines are the largest part of the gap.

Context
- The gap is not the result of a single day: A was ahead of B on every day of July except 2 July and 8 July. The same order holds in the rest of the data for this segment: June (A 80.0%, B 77.2%) and 1-29 August (A 80.1%, B 76.7%).
- The change log lists two changes affecting Mexico between 21 June and 31 July 2026: CHG-0702 (2 July, 09:00 local), routing v13 sending 10% of MX debit traffic to Acquirer C (logged as an A/B test), and CHG-0728 (28 July, 10:00 local), a 3DS SDK upgrade on web checkout (MX and CO). Payments routed first to C are attributed to C, so they are not in the A and B figures above.

What I did not check
- Why B is lower (decline codes, issuer, card brand, merchant segment or routing-version mix), so I am not naming a cause. The 3.4 pp is the observed difference on the traffic each acquirer received, not proof of a performance difference on identical traffic.
- Whether either change above has any footprint on A's or B's first-attempt rate.

questions.question: Was there any early warning before the Colombia debit incident of 13 August 2026?
questions.answer:
Short answer: yes, but not in the debit KPIs. The daily anomaly detector fired only on the day itself. The early warning was in the cascade-alert table and the change log, 7 days earlier, on the acquirer that debit traffic was later moved to.

Incident window (Bogota time): 13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10, taken from routing change CHG-0813 (100% of CO domestic debit to Acquirer B) and its rollback CHG-0814. Hourly data confirms the start: the 14:00 hour was 100% on B at 73.2% final approval (56 payments), against 85.7% in the 13:00 hour on A (77 payments). Hourly rows after 14 Aug 01:00 were not returned, so the end rests on the rollback entry. Whole day 13 Aug (CO, debit, domestic): 79.4% vs an 86.7% 28-day baseline, -7.3 pp.

What gave early warning
- Cascade alerts (Colombia, 1 Jun to 16 Aug checked): Acquirer B, code 05 Do not honor, was flagged every day from 6 to 12 Aug. Retry rate was 5.0% on 6 Aug (1 of 20 failures) and 0.0% on 7-12 Aug (14 to 27 failures a day), against a 100.0% healthy baseline.
- Change log: CHG-0806 (6 Aug 08:00) deployed decline mapping v2.3 for Acquirer B, described only as 'adds R65 handling'. The data shows another effect: the B/05 retry collapse starts the same day. On 13 Aug, B/05 under v2.3 was mapped as hard with 0.0% cascade, while A/05 in the 14 days before had 98.4% cascade and 21.3% recovery. CHG-0815 (15 Aug) later reclassified R05 as soft and retryable.
- No external notice for Colombia between 1 Jul and 15 Aug (the only one, EXT-0721, is for Brazil).

What gave no warning
- Anomaly table (CO debit, 14 Jul to 12 Aug): no day flagged. Worst dip was -1.9 pp on 9 Aug (84.8% vs 86.7%). First flag: 13 Aug (z_binomial -7.32).
- Debit on A looked normal until the change: 13 Aug 07:00-13:59 hourly rates were 83.0% to 88.6% (35 to 87 payments an hour). A's daily p95 latency stayed between 1,155 and 1,298 ms and technical failures between 2 and 16 a day (14 Jul to 12 Aug).

Cause (checked on whole-day 13 Aug, see limits): the drivers table puts the drop on Acquirer B / routing v14 (647 payments at 74.3%, -6.86 pp; A had 503 at 85.9%, -0.28 pp). The largest decline increase was B/05, 93 failures, +8.09 pp of payments, none retried. That is acquirer/mapping side, which a retry can recover, not one issuer: effects are spread over all eight issuers (largest CO-ISS-01, -1.65 pp).

Limits
- The alert table has no card-type split. Domestic debit had no payments on B before 13 Aug 14:00, so the 6-12 Aug signal came from other Colombian traffic (not identified). It warned about B's mapping, not about the debit rate.
- Drivers, decline shift and cascade health were run on the whole of 13 Aug, not on the 14:00-12:10 window. I did not size lost approvals or USD.

Recommended action
1. Before moving a segment to an acquirer, check that acquirer's cascade alerts: B/05 had been red for 7 days when v14 shipped.
2. Page on is_alert rows, and watch hourly approval after any routing change; the drop was visible in the first hour.
3. Require a data footprint check on mapping changes, since descriptions can omit effects. After hotfix v2.3.1 there is no B/05 alert row on 15 or 16 Aug; confirm retries on B before attempting v14 again.

**CO-ISS-07 had the lowest final approval: 65.3% (47 approved of 72 payments sent).**

Window: 13 Aug 2026 14:00 to 14 Aug 2026 12:10, Colombia local time (start inclusive, end exclusive). Segment: domestic debit cards (is_cross_border = false) issued by Colombian issuers. Final approval = final approved / payments sent, so it includes approvals recovered by a cascade. The whole segment was 75.6% on 1,004 payments sent.

| Issuer | Payments sent | Final approved | Final approval (window) | 95% margin | 14-day baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CO-ISS-07 | 72 | 47 | 65.3% | ±11.0 pp | 84.9% |
| CO-ISS-03 | 145 | 105 | 72.4% | ±7.3 pp | 84.8% |
| CO-ISS-05 | 96 | 70 | 72.9% | ±8.9 pp | 84.6% |
| CO-ISS-02 | 169 | 126 | 74.6% | ±6.6 pp | 87.9% |
| CO-ISS-04 | 110 | 84 | 76.4% | ±7.9 pp | 86.1% |
| CO-ISS-06 | 118 | 91 | 77.1% | ±7.6 pp | 87.0% |
| CO-ISS-01 | 230 | 184 | 80.0% | ±5.2 pp | 87.8% |
| CO-ISS-08 | 64 | 52 | 81.3% | ±9.6 pp | 87.0% |

How to read it:
- Small sample. CO-ISS-07 had only 72 payments, so its rate carries an approximate 95% margin of ±11.0 pp. Its gap to CO-ISS-03 (72.4%) and CO-ISS-05 (72.9%) is smaller than that margin, so it is the lowest on the point estimate, but the order among the lowest three is not firm.
- The drop was not limited to this issuer. All eight issuers were below their own 14-day baseline in the window, and the segment as a whole was 10.95 pp below its baseline. CO-ISS-07 fell furthest against its own baseline (84.9% to 65.3%), but with only 72 payments it accounts for -1.41 pp of the segment drop. CO-ISS-02 accounts for the most (-2.25 pp), then CO-ISS-03 and CO-ISS-01 (-1.8 pp each).
- Timing of changes (Colombia change log, 3 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10 Bogota time): CHG-0813 on 13 Aug at 14:00, exactly at the window start, routing v14 sending 100% of CO domestic debit to Acquirer B; and CHG-0806 on 6 Aug at 08:00, decline-code mapping v2.3 for Acquirer B (adds R65 handling). I am flagging timing only. I have not tested whether either explains the drop.

Cross-checks: for the whole hours 14:00 to 12:00, silver_payments and gold_approval_hourly both give 987 payments sent and 746 final approvals, and the per-issuer volumes and rates match fn_approval_drivers. Hourly final approval for this segment was 85.7% in the 13:00 hour on 13 Aug, 73.2% in the 14:00 hour and 84.6% in the 12:00 hour on 14 Aug.

Not run, so I am not stating a cause: impact sizing (fn_drop_impact), acquirer and routing-version drivers, decline-code shift, cascade health, and any change after 12:10. Since every issuer fell, I would start with the acquirer and routing-version split. I can run those next.
